hook: "op-SEHK": a little table holds the open condolence book and a vase of white lilies for the OBSEQUIES: OBSEQUIES
note: Les obsèques (always plural, feminine) are a funeral, the formal word used in notices and invitations (les obsèques auront lieu mardi). English obsequies is the same word.

room_name: Le portail du cimetière · The churchyard gate
change: added (new vocab entry, EGLISE2 manual)
hook: "few-nay-RYE": a calm FUNERAL procession: a few adults in dark clothes walk slowly along the path, each holding white flowers: FUNERAL
note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Les funérailles (always plural, feminine) are a funeral, formal word: des funérailles nationales (a state funeral).

room_name: Le portail du cimetière · The churchyard gate
change: added (street verb rehomed; Monsieur Verbe mime, beret by conjugation group); vocab room ST_social_seg007 -> R_ch_cemetery
hook: "ruh-kuh-YEER": Monsieur Verbe gathers up the white flowers fallen on the path into a neat little bouquet: to collect (recueillir): RE-COLLECT
note: Recueillir = to collect, to gather (recueillir des signatures, des dons); to take in (recueillir un chat abandonné). Se recueillir = to pause in quiet reflection or prayer (se recueillir sur une tombe). Irregular like cueillir: je recueille. English recollect has the same Latin root. [say override: ruh-kuh-YEER]

room_name: Le portail du cimetière · The churchyard gate
change: added (new vocab entry, EGLISE2 manual)
hook: "ahn-tehr-MAHN": the prepared grave for the burial (INTERMENT) is covered with a neat green cloth and ringed with flower wreaths on stands: INTERMENT
note: L'enterrement is a burial, a funeral (aller à un enterrement); from enterrer = to bury, en + terre (earth), like English interment. Un enterrement de vie de garçon: a bachelor party.

room_name: Le portail du cimetière · The churchyard gate
change: added (new vocab entry, EGLISE2 manual)
hook: "sehr-KUHY": the closed polished wooden COFFIN, covered with a big spray of white roses, rests calmly on its wheeled stand: COFFIN
note: Le cercueil is a coffin, a casket (mettre en bière = to place in the coffin). It comes from the same Greek word as English sarcophagus.

room_name: Le portail du cimetière · The churchyard gate
change: added (new vocab entry, EGLISE2 manual)
hook: "kor-bee-YAHR": the long dark HEARSE waits calmly by the churchyard gate, its back door open on a bed of white flowers: HEARSE
note: Le corbillard is a hearse. The name comes from the corbillats, the old passenger boats of the town of Corbeil. [say override: kor-bee-YAHR]

room_name: Le portail du cimetière · The churchyard gate
change: added (EGLISE2b: new vocab entry, manual, plain picture painted in by crop-edit)
hook: "DYAHKR": a calm young DEACON in a long white alb, his red-and-gold stole worn across his chest like a sash, reads quietly from an open book by the churchyard gate: DEACON
note: This is a cognate: diacre and deacon come from the same Greek word (diakonos, servant), so the picture simply shows it. Un diacre is a deacon; a deacon wears his stole diagonally, from the left shoulder to the right hip.
